model: TB3026B / TB3026B-W BACnet FF fixed-function thermostat
applies_to: Honeywell TB3026B and TB3026B-W BACnet FF wall-mount fixed-function thermostats, all 19 built-in applications (platform objects).
summary: The BACnet FF (TB3026B) is a fixed-function thermostat/controller on BACnet MS/TP that runs one of 19 built-in applications (fan coils, heat pumps, unit ventilators and others). This list is the platform's ordered list of named control points: setpoints and limits, displayed and sensed values, occupancy and schedule control, maintenance timers, humidity setpoints and the many screen-control objects. The application in use adds its own AV 0-89 / BV 0-63 points, documented per application in the guide.
notes: The appendix gives each object a label in an 'Object Name' column, but its property tables say the Object_Name property reads 'AV-nnn' / 'BV-nnn' / 'MV-nnn' for most objects. The labels are used as names here; a scan may show the AV-nnn form.
Physical I/O objects (AI 0-2, AO 0-7, BI 0-2, BO 0-5) and the general-use AV 0-89 / BV 0-63 depend on the loaded application (DDC file); they are not listed here except where the guide names them.
BV 40 (general-use range) is the occupancy command and supports a priority array.
Access comes from the appendix where it has an access column; otherwise it is inferred (displayed/sensed/current/status points and multistates read-only, others writable).
Taken from Appendix B (ordered list of control points) with access and descriptions from Appendix A of the guide.

source.title: BACnet FF Installation and Operations Guide

integration.summary: Set the MS/TP MAC and device instance in the ISU menu, then write occupancy (BV 40, or let the internal schedule run) and the occupied setpoint AV 90. Read the sensed room temperature, the active heating/cooling setpoints and the occupied status. Application-specific outputs and alarms are in the per-application tables of the guide.
integration.enable: Occupancy comes from BV 40 (priority array) or the internal schedule (BV 133).
setup: Factory defaults: MS/TP MAC 0 (valid 0-127), device instance 0009999 (valid 0-4194302).
MS/TP MAC and device instance are set through ISU parameters on the thermostat.
Application selection is an ISU / setup setting; it decides which AV 0-89 / BV 0-63 points are used.
gotchas: Many BVs and AVs above 200 only control the display layout; do not map them for HVAC control.
